notes.text: Given me — This and the following passages may be in some sort understood of the prophet Isaiah, but they are far more evidently and eminently verified in Christ, and indeed seem to be meant directly of him. The tongue - All ability of speaking plainly, and convincingly, and persuasively. Weary - Burdened with the sense of his, deplorable condition. Wakeneth - Me, from time to time, and continually. To hear - He by his Divine power assists me to the practice of all his commands and my duties, with all attention and diligence.
I gave — I patiently yielded up myself to those who smote me.

Justifieth — God will clear up my righteousness, and shew by many and mighty signs and wonders, that I lived and died his faithful servant. Let him come - l am conscious of mine own innocency, and I know that God will give sentence for me.
They — Mine accusers and enemies. The moth - Shall be cut off and consumed by a secret curse.

glossa.text: *The Lord hath given,* etc. ((ID.)) Although these things can be referred to Isaias, yet properly they are referred to Christ, as though he said: I who once wrought such things can now also work the like; my power is not diminished.

*As a garment.* ((ID.)) A garment is consumed by age and by the moth. The Jews too were called to penance for forty-two years after the Passion: at last, being negligent, they were crushed when the Romans came, and devoured by the moth of an evil conscience.

*O God, unto my help.* He urges that we glory in God, not in ourselves. ((CAS.)) Here every petition is an affirmation, whence tribulations are not to be feared. This little verse is said beforehand at the beginning of all the hours, because, when we are wont to pray, the devil strives most of all to tempt us, so that dying flies may spoil the sweetness of the ointment.

*Let them be confounded.* ((CAS.)) To be confounded is to be troubled over one's perversity. *Let them be ashamed,* lest punishment, an offspring from justice, follow them. *That seek,* etc. ((AUG.)) The times in the Church are diverse: first there was the onset of persecutors, whence, *that seek;* now there remains the ill will of those who plot, whence, *that will.* ((ID.))
*Let them be turned backward.* ((ID.)) There are two kinds of persecutors, etc., *as far as* he comes forth whole who is caught by neither.

*Let all rejoice and be glad in thee.* ((CAS.)) He urges the good to be glad, whom, being needy, God helps and delivers. *Always.* Because he ought not ever to cease from his praise. *Let God be magnified.* ((CAS.)) Said after our manner, where one grows by praises; for it is not God, but we, who by praising make progress.

*But I am needy.* ((CAS.)) What I exhort, I do, etc., *as far as* where he is rich, he ever goes about, desires and receives. *Delay not.* ((ID.)) That seems slow which is sought with great desire. ((AUG.)) Lest what thou art to come should seem to me too slow — which comes about through patience; and he who lacks it, to him it seems slow, and he is turned aside from it: like Lot's wife, who became a pillar of salt, that she might season thee: for she is an example to thee, that thou look not back.

notes.text: Wherefore, being encompassed with a cloud — A great multitude, tending upward with a holy swiftness. Of witnesses - Of the power of faith. Let us lay aside every weight - As all who run a race take care to do. Let us throw off whatever weighs us down, or damps the vigour of our Soul. And the sin which easily besetteth us - As doth the sin of our constitution, the sin of our education, the sin of our profession.

Looking — From all other things. To Jesus - As the wounded Israelites to the brazen serpent. Our crucified Lord was prefigured by the lifting up of this; our guilt, by the stings of the fiery serpents; and our faith, by their looking up to the miraculous remedy. The author and finisher of our faith - Who begins it in us, carries it on, and perfects it. Who for the joy that was set before him - Patiently and willingly endured the cross, with all the pains annexed thereto. And is set down - Where there is fulness of joy.

Consider — Draw the comparison and think. The Lord bore all this; and shall his servants bear nothing? Him that endured such contradiction from sinners - Such enmity and opposition of every kind Lest ye be weary - Dull and languid, and so actually faint in your course.

glossa.text: *And therefore we also.* After the commendation of faith, he returns to that which he had begun, exhorting to patience in many ways, and chiefly by the example of Christ himself. *A cloud.* That is, the multitude of the saints, who are witnesses of faith, who as clouds refresh us by their own example in the heat of tribulations, and rain upon us with their doctrines.

*Who, having joy set before him,* etc. So ought we, eternal joy being set before us and confusion set aside, to run; or, joy of a temporal kingdom being set before him, when the crowds wished to take him by force to make him king, and he would not, because it was the way of humility.
*Fainting.* To faint is, through fear of tribulation, to deny the faith. Therefore you ought not to faint, for neither have you forgotten the consolation, nor ought you to forget it.

notes.text: One of you — The speaking thus indefinitely at first was profitable to them all.

There was lying in the bosom of Jesus -- that is, sitting next to him at table. This phrase only expresses the then customary posture at meals, where the guests all leaned sidewise on couches. And each was said to lie in the bosom of him who was placed next above him. One of the disciples whom Jesus loved — St. John avoids with great care the expressly naming himself. Perhaps our Lord now gave him the first proof of his peculiar love, by disclosing this secret to him.
Simon Peter — Behind Jesus, who lay between them.
Leaning down, and so asking him privately.

Jesus answered — In his ear. So careful was he not to offend (if it had been possible) even Judas himself. The sop - Which he took up while he was speaking. He giveth it to Judas - And probably the other disciples thought Judas peculiarly happy! But when even this instance of our Lord's tenderness could not move him, then Satan took full possession.

What thou doest, do quickly — This is not a permission, much less a command. It is only as if he had said, If thou art determined to do it, why dost thou delay? Hereby showing Judas, that he could not be hid, and expressing his own readiness to suffer.
None knew why he said this — Save John and Judas.
He went out — To the chief priests. But he returned afterward, and was with them when they ate the passover, Matt. xxvi, 20, though not at the Lord's Supper.

Jesus saith — Namely, the next day; on Thursday, in the morning. Here the scene, as it were, is opened, for the discourse which is continued in the following chapters. Now - While I speak this, the Son of man is glorified - Being fully entered into his glorious work of redemption. This evidently relates to the glory which belongs to his suffering in so holy and victorious a manner.

glossa.text: *When Jesus had said these things* Our infirmity was truly troubled in him, not his own power, as it also truly suffered. But he willingly took the trouble upon himself, lest the servant troubled by necessity should despair. And that he is troubled signifies that spiritual men are to be troubled out of charity, when an urgent cause is compelled to separate even the cockle from the wheat before the harvest.

*And when he had dipped the bread.* The dipping of the bread signifies the feigning of Judas, who came to the supper a feigned friend. For the things that are dipped are not cleansed but stained. But if the dipping signifies something good, damnation not undeservedly followed one ungrateful to that same good. *He gave it to Judas, son of Simon the Iscariot,* etc. Not, as some think, did Judas now receive the body of Christ. For it must be known that the Lord had already distributed to all the sacrament of his body and blood, among whom Judas also was; then by the dipped morsel the traitor himself is pointed out, etc.

*That which thou dost.* He did not command, but he foretells evil to Judas, good to us, because he wills this to be done quickly, not so much hastening to that man's punishment as to the salvation of the faithful.

*Because he had the purse.* In which the offerings were examined for the needs of their own and of others in want. Wherein a form is given to the Church of keeping what is necessary, which is bidden not to think of the morrow, lest it serve for earthly things, or through fear of want forsake justice.

*And it was.* The night befits the sacrament. For he who went out was a son of darkness, doing the works of darkness.

*Now is the Son of man glorified. ((AUG.))* Judas going out, for whom it was said: *You are not all clean,* etc., *as far as* as though that were already done which is soon to be.

registers.label: Spare
lines: He gave the bread to the one who would betray him.
And it was night.
Be pleased, O God, to deliver us; make haste to help us.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
We run with endurance the race set before us.
Looking to Jesus, who endured the cross.
Come, let us worship as the shadows fall.
Do not be far from us, O Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: At the table he is troubled in spirit, and he takes a piece of bread, dips it, and hands it to the one who will sell him.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
The friend takes the morsel and rises and goes out, and the gospel says only this: and it was night.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
Make haste, O God, to deliver us; you are our help and our deliverer; do not delay.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
Around us hangs a great cloud of witnesses; lay aside every weight, and run the race set before you.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
Look to Jesus, who for the joy set before him endured the cross. Come, let us worship as night comes on.
Do not be far from us, O Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: He hands the bread to the one who will betray him; it was night.

Make haste, O God, to help us; do not delay.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
Surrounded by a cloud of witnesses, we run the race.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
Looking to Jesus, come, let us worship.
Do not be far from us, O Lord. Amen.
